claim: Why high contrast makes it work: 'the object's edge rides a black line' — a sharp cut hidden inside the ink is invisible, seams are hidden by occlusion, not blur, and 'the soft, smeary masks we started with were a confession that we didn't have the real edge yet'.

pieces.section: Why high contrast makes it work
pieces.what: One inked plate cut two ways — soft feathered mask vs hard cut on the black line — then slid a few pixels apart: the feather shows a halo, the black-line cut disappears.

pieces.section: The two contraries — the flat stack and the break
pieces.what: The track-VI plates as a parallax stack: tilt to reveal the air between sheets (reveal the stack), then a button that lets one sheet tear loose into depth (break the stack).

pieces.section: The A/B duals — choose by what you hold
pieces.what: The separate route and the generate route on the same scene side by side, with coherence and alpha quality marked — the duals table shown in its own evidence.
A dialogue balloon placed at three stack depths — behind the figure, at the speaker's depth, on top — and drifting with its speaker on a camera move.
